content.text:
I submitted **index 6 (Sb fraction 0.2115)**. It gave the highest EQE I measured, 0.149%, but it's the best of only five points, so I can't confirm it's the true best on the line.

I used all 5 EQE measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.138 | 0.061 |
| **6** | **0.2115** | **0.149** |
| 7 | 0.2325 | 0.124 |
| 15 | 0.507 | 0.048 |
| 23 | 0.755 | 0.021 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is highest at the low-Sb end and falls steadily as Sb increases. Index 6 sits almost exactly at the composition of the known In11Sb3O24 phase (Sb 0.214), and EQE drops on both sides of it.
- **What I didn't cover:** Five points can't pin the peak down. Indices 0, 2–5 and 8–10 were never measured, so a composition near Sb 0.20 or Sb 0.25–0.28 could still be slightly better.
- **XRD:** I used 2 of 5 XRD scans, on indices 5 and 7. They gave nearly identical patterns, but comparing them to the simulated phases (In11Sb3O24, In2O3 and InSbO4) was inconclusive: similarities were only 0.23–0.34. So I can't confirm which phase is actually present, and the choice rests on the EQE numbers.
